content.intro: This lesson covers Advanced Business Analysis as part of Professional Spreadsheet Engineering and Specialized Applications. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Advanced Business Analysis contributes to reliable business reporting and professional spreadsheet delivery. Document assumptions, verify results independently, and separate optional platform tools from core Excel behavior. Compatibility: Power Query, the Data Model, Power Pivot and DAX are related but distinct capabilities; their exact availability varies by Excel edition, operating system, license and update channel. Follow the course’s local availability checklist before building a dependent workflow.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced Business Analysis focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Combining multiple data sources; KPI definitions and measurement; Segmentation and trend analysis; Reporting conclusions without overstating evidence. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: Measure expression for total amount in a Data Model table named Sales with a numeric Amount column. The table and column names must match the model.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Create a measure in the Data Model/Power Pivot measure editor, then compare it with an independently calculated total. Availability varies by Excel edition/platform.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for advanced business analysis. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates advanced business analysis. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates advanced business analysis; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Measure expression for total amount in a Data Model table named Sales with a numeric Amount column. The table and column names must match the model.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
summary: Advanced Business Analysis supports the workflow in Professional Spreadsheet Engineering and Specialized Applications.
Use a small example, make assumptions visible, and verify the result against the source.
Check target-version availability and keep a clean copy before making high-impact changes.
